beats.note: However, encryption does not solve every security problem.
It cannot protect data from a person who already has authorized access,
and it cannot prevent every type of malware, phishing attack, or social-engineering attack.
Encryption protects information, but the surrounding systems and users must also be secure.
Overall, encryption supports three major security goals: confidentiality, integrity, and authentication.
It helps keep information private, helps detect unauthorized changes, and can help verify the identity of the people or systems involved.
As more communication, commerce, and personal activity move online, encryption has become a fundamental part of modern computer science and cybersecurity.
